  PROBLEM: The guard-hook fallthrough condition does not exclude `_gl_resolved`/`_gl_defer_commit`. On an `orchestrator/project-*` head whose conflicts are one paired guard hook plus `.gitleaksignore`, `_ghm_defer_commit` stays false, so the else branch calls `_conflict_prepare_commit_deterministic_merge "Guard-hook template merge"`, which commits and runs `exit 0` before the `.gitleaksignore` deferral (1204-1213) and the integration fingerprint check / deferred commit (1763-1881) are reached.
  WHY: The integration-sync merge is committed and pushed without the fingerprint check that the issue, README and agents fragment promise, and this conflict mix previously failed closed with `sandbox_path_host_only`. The test harness hard-codes `_ghm_resolved=false`, so no test covers this. Suggested fix: add `&& [ "${_gl_resolved:-false}" != "true" ]` to the condition, plus a guard-hook + `.gitleaksignore` integration test. All reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:302-308 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The gitleaks suggestion path checks each fingerprint's commit with `git cat-file -e` / `merge-base --is-ancestor` against the shallow checkout (`.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2223`, `fetch-depth: 100`) and never deepens history, so a valid fingerprint naming an ancestor more than 100 commits back is dropped silently.
  WHY: On the long-lived `orchestrator/project-*` heads the feature targets, the escalation comment leaves out the required ready-to-paste fingerprint lines, and the log line `REVIEW_EDITOR_GITLEAKS_SUGGESTION ... outcome=none count=0` looks the same as "no gitleaks output". Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT and the other four rated it MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:664-665, 1813-1815, 2136-2138 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_triage_superseded_note` treats an empty `tracking_issue` as proof that the issue is standalone and does not also exclude the `ai:orchestrator-managed` label. A managed check-triage issue with a missing or malformed `Tracking issue:` line therefore gets the superseded note and returns early.
  WHY: This breaks the requirement that orchestrator items stay unchanged: the managed item skips its normal judge verdict for that run. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 checked this claim and did not carry it forward, saying it depends on a malformed managed issue and shares the existing `[ -z "${tracking_issue}" ]` predicate used at lines 614 and 2141.
- scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:1791-1798 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The fingerprint re-expansion exemption drops every verifier violation on `.gitleaksignore`, including must_not_contain violations.
  WHY: A merge that violates the integration-sync fingerprint contract can proceed with no violation on record. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same issue only as hardening suggestions: emit `::warning::` instead of `::notice::`.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:553-558, 667-679 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The new path treats a cached `status=disabled` from the check-triage resolution gate as a non-resolved verdict and posts the superseded note.
  WHY: When `CHECK_TRIAGE_RESOLVED_GATE_ENABLED=false`, the gate returns `status=disabled` with exit code 0, which is cached, so normal judging is suppressed even though the issue requires gate-off cases to judge as before.
